# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking.**

Let me trace who can reach whom. I can't speak, so my only outbound is gesture — and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind can speak, and I can hear, so Blind can talk *to* me but can never hear an answer... except through one loophole: a blind recipient of a gesture receives one blank per symbol. That means the *count* of symbols I send to="blind" is a number channel Blind can read. So the full loop is: Deaf sees the bomb and signs me the light colour → I look up the table → I count out the answer to Blind in blanks. For that, Blind needs to propose a numbering scheme aloud (I'll hear it next round), and Deaf needs to tell me the light colour now.

My manual: printed things are bait; the real input is the light. Light blue → cut yellow, light green → cut green, light red → cut blue.

First move: ping Blind with exactly one blank, so they discover the channel exists and can set up a counting code in their speech this round. Second: open negotiations with Deaf — I propose reading-order (alphabetical: blue=1, green=2, red=3) finger-counts, topic "light" (pantomimed as a snap/spark), and ask them to reply. Deaf is clever; if my guess at pantomime misses, I'll refine from whatever they sign back.

```
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫰", "✍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫴"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here — I can hear you, but I never receive gestures, so your sign to me arrived as nothing. Your only road to me is through Deaf: sign to Deaf, and Deaf will read your signs aloud to me. Deaf hears nothing, so signs are your only words to Deaf. What my hands find on the bomb: a display whose content I cannot feel, a light whose state I cannot feel, one large button with embossed letters reading PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, with no colours I can feel. Please find everything the manual says about displays, indicator lights, buttons labelled push to defuse, and cutting wires. Deaf sees the wire colours, the display and the light. Ask Deaf to define a sign code out loud, one sign per letter or per common word, so all three of us learn it; then spell the rules to Deaf and Deaf will relay them to me by voice. Confirm you heard me by signing a thumbs up to Deaf. I will touch nothing until the manual clears it.
Deaf says: This is Deaf speaking, so you both hear me. I can see the bomb, I can never hear anyone, and I cannot touch it. Since I speak last each round, you get this at the start of the next one. Full view of the bomb: display reads zero. One indicator light, and it is blue. One large button printed with the words: push to defuse. Three wires: wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow, and I read them as numbered left to right. Nothing else is printed on it. Mute, I saw your seven gestures. I guess the pointing hands meant wire one, wire two, wire three, and the writing hand meant the manual. From now on answer me like this: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, one, two, three fingers mean wire one, two, three, the writing hand means the manual, open palm up means you are asking me a question. Whatever you sign to me, I will say out loud so Blind hears it too. Blind, I saw your wave. You can speak to Mute directly and Mute will hear you, but Mute cannot answer you except through me, and I cannot hear you, so if you ever need to tell me something, gesture it and I will see it. Mute, please look up whatever the manual says about a zero display, a blue light, a large push-to-defuse button, and three wires that are blue, green, yellow in that order, and confirm or correct my reading of your gestures.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

**Thinking.**

The picture is nearly complete. Manual: everything printed is bait — the display's "zero" and the button's "PUSH TO DEFUSE" label are both traps; the button must never be pressed. The only way out is the light→wire table. Deaf reports the light is blue, so the answer right now is: cut the yellow wire, which is wire three (1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow). But Blind must not act until the instruction is relayed, and Blind needs the full table in case the light changes.

My only outbound is gesture to Deaf, who can voice it for Blind. Deaf gave me six signs (👍 👎, wires 1-2-3, ✍ manual, 🫴 question). I'll extend it with three self-evident ones and state the grammar in the structure: ✊ = a fist striking = "press the button"; 🫰 = my snap from turn one, now clearly paired = "the light"; 🤌 = pinched fingers = "cut". Grammar: a finger-count immediately after 🫰 is the light's colour alphabetically (1 blue, 2 green, 3 red); a finger-count after 🤌 is the wire number left to right (1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow).

Sequence one confirms to Deaf and Blind that the channel works and I heard everything. Sequence two is the urgent one: manual says thumbs-down to the fist — do not press the button. The last three are the full table: light blue → cut wire three, light green → cut wire two, light red → cut wire one. Even if Deaf can't fully parse the grammar yet, they see the blue light themselves and know wire three is yellow — hearing "manual, light, one, cut, three" while looking at a blue light should let them and Blind crack it, and Blind can lock the grammar aloud next round for me to confirm or correct sign by sign.
